title: Organizations use AI to redesign work, but earnings lag
evidence: Organizations use AI across business workflows, with 80% reporting individual productivity gains but only 37% reporting positive enterprise EBIT impact.
scoring_reason: Actual enterprise AI use, workflow redesign and measured productivity and earnings consequences.

title: Japanese companies use AI narrowly rather than company-wide
evidence: Japanese companies use AI in limited operations: 16% have deployed it company-wide, while 60% use it only in parts of the business.
scoring_reason: Actual company AI adoption across operations with measured deployment depth and budget consequences.

title: Companies are wiring AI into legacy business systems
evidence: Companies are deploying AI across finance, procurement, supply-chain and HR workflows, increasing demand for integration, permissions, audit trails and data governance.
scoring_reason: Actual enterprise AI deployment changes core operating processes and implementation spending.

title: Professional-services teams embed AI but struggle to sell the value
evidence: Professional-services teams using AI daily across legal work were nine times more likely to report significant efficiency and quality gains than minimal users.
scoring_reason: Actual workplace AI use changes legal delivery, efficiency, quality, pricing and client conversations.

title: Advertisers use AI at scale as disclosure rules tighten
evidence: Advertising companies used AI in the creative process at scale: 83% of ad executives reported use, up 23 percentage points from 2024.
scoring_reason: Actual AI use in marketing production changes disclosure, creative workflow and customer trust.

title: Customer-service AI adoption is racing ahead of value
evidence: Organizations adopted AI in customer-service workflows at a 70% rate, yet only 2% reported improved outcomes and return on investment.
scoring_reason: Actual organizational AI use in customer service reveals a measured process and ROI gap.

title: Google launches a regulated AI research agent shaped by Deutsche Bank
evidence: Google Cloud launched an AI-powered financial research agent designed with Deutsche Bank to reduce manual research and improve auditability and client preparation.
scoring_reason: A real AI industry launch has direct consequences for regulated banking research, governance and client work.

title: Retailers deploy AI agents into sales and customer service
evidence: Retailers deployed AI agents in sales and customer-service workflows, recording 8% year-on-year sales growth versus 2% without agents.
scoring_reason: Vendor-owned production data links actual retail AI deployment to sales and service outcomes.

title: Customer-service leaders shift budgets toward AI
evidence: Customer-service leaders increased AI investment 38% while total function budgets grew 2%, changing the balance between labour, overhead and technology.
scoring_reason: A measured AI investment shift has direct cost, workforce and service-delivery consequences.

title: Procurement teams use AI weekly but struggle to scale workflows
evidence: Procurement teams use AI for spend analysis, contracts and supplier decisions: 49% ran pilots, but only 4% reached large-scale deployment.
scoring_reason: Actual AI use changes procurement work, productivity, risk and decision quality, but production scale remains rare.
